name: Dar Al Hadaya
note: Recorded domain drupaledi.com is a dead Drupal dev domain (DNS fails), and the 'furniture manufacturing' reason is wrong: the real business is Dar Al Hadaya, an established Saudi home-accessories and soft-furnishings retailer since 1969 operating a live online store at al-hadaya.com with customer accounts and first-order offers. Live cart confirmation was WAF-blocked (429) but retailer identity and e-commerce are well documented.

name: Maan Aljasser & Co.
note: Industrial group (steel recycling/fabrication plus custom wood furniture); its consumer brand Creative Closets sells built-in closets and bespoke bedrooms via a measure-design-install project model (Gate 2 cabinetry/installation exclusion) with low repeat frequency, not a product-retail catalog.

name: TIMBER HOUSE- بيت الاخشاب
note: Small Riyadh furniture/home-furnishings manufacturer (~20 staff) making bedrooms, wardrobes and wooden decor with customization plus distribution; only an Instagram presence, no live transactional store or multi-store retail chain found.

name: Abouseoud Furniture Factories Co.
note: Jeddah furniture and woodwork manufacturer since 1978; site shows 'Website Under Updation, Coming Soon' and sources describe it as primarily a manufacturer, not a retail-showroom or consumer e-commerce operation.

name: Elite Lines Factory
note: Identified only as a Saudi furniture factory (LinkedIn: elitelinessa); site persistently returned 503 and no dedicated consumer retail arm or e-commerce was found, so it defaults OUT per the verification protocol.

name: AL MOUSA Co. Ltd.
note: Excluded on contracting/wholesale/engineering NAICS, but Al-Mousa runs Woody (woody.com.sa), a live consumer furniture store with hundreds of SKUs, SAR pricing, working cart/checkout and multiple showroom branches, HQ Riyadh. Classic Lazurde pattern: substantial dedicated retail alongside the B2B/manufacturing line.

name: Saudi Damons
note: Chinese-invested Saudi furniture factory producing office/executive/workstation furniture; its own stated vision is to supply 'furniture dealers and project contractors,' i.e. a B2B/project manufacturer, not a dedicated consumer retail operation.

name: hindalmujahed
note: Interior-design and implementation group with in-house carpet and wood factories (bespoke fit-out model); the storefront currently shows 'store is closed,' and core activity is interior design plus manufacturing (Gate 2 exclusions), with carpets also a narrow low-repeat category.

name: Sawaed Wood Industries Co.
note: Furniture manufacturer running five factories (four in Riyadh, one in Egypt, 75,000 sqm) described as an interior-furniture producer; a B2B/project manufacturer with no consumer retail arm or e-commerce found.

name: SAUDI FITOUT
note: B2B fit-out contractor with woodwork manufacturing and FF&E procurement divisions serving hotels, hospitals and offices; a corporate/portfolio site with no cart or consumer retail, squarely in the Gate 2 fit-out/contracting exclusion.

name: BTT furniture & construction
note: The 'construction' name-pattern reason is wrong: Badael Tech is a furniture business (office, educational, home, hospitality) with showrooms in Riyadh and the Eastern Province. However no functional consumer cart or pricing was visible and the emphasis is B2B 'workspace solutions,' so a real transactional retail channel is unconfirmed.

name: AAF GROUP
note: The pure-manufacturing NAICS exclusion is doubtful: this appears to be Al Farhoud Furniture Group (family-owned since 1979) offering 'furniture for all segments' with its own brands (Lilt, Miro, Attallah), i.e. consumer-furniture-aligned. With no domain on file, showroom count, live e-commerce and scale could not be confirmed.

name: Qatar Living
note: A Qatar classifieds/community/news portal (properties, vehicles, jobs, services), not a product retailer, so the non-retail category call is defensible. But it operates a popular consumer iOS/Android app that could trigger the Gate 5b 50k+ download app-rescue; the download count could not be confirmed and its classifieds/media nature versus the intended commerce-app carve-out is genuinely ambiguous.

name: foamco.sa
note: Recorded domain abulessafactory.com is dead (DNS fails), but the business (Abu Lessa foam/mattress factory, est. 2013) trades live at foamco.com.sa as a broad home-furniture retailer: ~180+ SKUs across 11+ categories (dining, bedroom, living, lighting, decor), SAR pricing and cart, made in and shipping across Saudi Arabia. Manufacturer plus substantial retail, not mattresses-only.

name: RAM International
note: Interior construction and fit-out contractor (est. 1999, Jeddah) offering design-build, MEP, FF&E and AV/security to government, hospitality and commercial clients; no online store or consumer retail, a Gate 2 B2B fit-out exclusion (the 'furniture manufacturing' reason was off but the outcome holds).

name: Al Dar Al Jameela
note: Qatar-based interior-design and furnishing company (est. 2006) working project-based with architects and developers on hotels, villas and offices with bespoke solutions; no consumer e-commerce or retail storefront, a Gate 2 interior-design/fit-out exclusion.

name: MAZ HOLDING
note: Excluded by a 'holding' name-pattern, but MAZ's core is consumer home-furnishings retail: Bed Quarter (26 showrooms since 1997; KING KOIL, TEMPUR, NOLTE, La-Z-Boy, OSIM) and Bed House (6 stores plus live e-commerce at bedhouse.com.sa), with in-house manufacturing as vertical integration (Aljazierah precedent). Qualifying basis is the retail arm; if strict Gate 6 parent-exclusion is applied, scope the row to Bed House/Bed Quarter. Live bedhouse.com.sa fetch was WAF-blocked (403) but its e-commerce is documented.

name: GUTHMI Group
note: Excluded on textile-manufacturing NAICS, but Al Guthmi is a fabric/textile retailer since 1942 with 24+ showrooms across Saudi Arabia selling upholstery, curtains and fabrics, plus an online 'Guthmi Store' at guthmi.net. Fabric/textile retail is an explicit Gate 3 pass and the multi-showroom footprint is substantial. Live-cart confirmation was WAF-blocked (403); flip rests on the documented retail footprint.

name: WISTER
note: Site persistently WAF-blocked (403) and search was unavailable; the only signals are data-processing, telecom and internet-publishing NAICS codes, indicating a tech/digital-services business with no consumer product retail, so it defaults OUT per the verification protocol. Low-confidence, not personally loaded.

name: Jamjoom General Agencies جمجوم للوكالات العامة
note: Site returned 503; the entity name ('General Agencies') and wholesale-distribution NAICS both denote a brand-agency/distribution business, and no dedicated consumer retail arm was found, so it defaults OUT. Not personally loaded.

name: Wasit Saudi Corp
note: Domain is dead (DNS fails) with no findable replacement site; NAICS point to education and amusement/recreation, not retail, so with no live storefront it defaults OUT per the verification protocol.

name: GCCTIC
note: 'Motabaqah' means conformity; this is a Gulf testing, inspection and certification (conformity-assessment) body (NAICS 54138 testing labs), a B2B services organization with no consumer retail.

name: Arab Center for Research and Policy Studies المركز العربي للأبحاث ودراسة السياسات
note: A Doha-based think tank / research institute publishing political and policy studies and hosting conferences; not a retailer in any sense.

name: Delicious Food Factory (DFF)
note: The brand Horayra is premium cat food made in Saudi Arabia (pet food is an approved category), but it carries only 2-3 SKUs and the site functions as an informational/community hub with no confirmed cart, failing the scale (~50+ SKU) and real-digital-channel gates regardless of the category.
